population.definition: Total population of Khomas Region at the 2023 Population and Housing Census (NSA). Windhoek is its urban core: press reports about 486,186 urban residents in the region (Windhoek Observer, urban definition not given). A Windhoek-only figure was not found in a readable official source.

source.title: Khomas – Namibia Statistics Agency | Census Disemination
source.quote: Total Population 494,605

facts.claim: Windhoek was founded on 18 October 1890, when Major Curt von François laid the foundation stone of the Alte Feste fort for the German protective corps (Schutztruppe).

source.title: History and Heritage
source.quote: The present Windhoek was founded on 18 October 1890 when Von Francois laid the foundation stone of the fort

facts.claim: The first recorded settlements grew up because of the hot springs; Nama and Herero names for the place referred to them.

source.title: History and Heritage
source.quote: The first recorded settlements were established because of the hot springs in the area.

facts.claim: The modern name is not settled: the city says some believe Jonker Afrikaner named it after the Winterhoek Mountains near Tulbagh, South Africa.

source.title: History and Heritage
source.quote: Some believe that Afrikaner named Windhoek after the Winterhoek Mountains near Tulbagh in South Africa

facts.claim: The Nama name /Ai-//Gams means Fire Water and the Herero name Otjomuise means Place of Steam; both referred to the hot springs.

source.title: History and Heritage
source.quote: "/Ai-//Gams" (Fire Water) by the Namas, and "Otjomuise" (Place of Steam) by the Hereros

facts.claim: Development quickened after 1907 as more settlers arrived from Germany and South Africa.

source.title: History and Heritage
source.quote: After 1907, the town developed more rapidly, with more settlers arriving from Germany and South Africa.

facts.claim: Windhoek is the capital of Namibia and is run by a municipality established under the Local Authority Act of 1992.

source.title: About Us
source.quote: Windhoek is the capital city of Namibia

timeline.claim: Orlam Captain Jan Jonker Afrikaner settles at the strongest spring in what is now Klein Windhoek.

source.title: History and Heritage
source.quote: the Orlam Captain, Jan Jonker Afrikaner, settled in at the strongest spring

timeline.claim: Von François lays the foundation stone of the fort; the city dates its founding to this day.

source.title: History and Heritage
source.quote: The present Windhoek was founded on 18 October 1890 when Von Francois laid the foundation stone of the fort

timeline.claim: During the 1904 Herero war the Alte Feste serves as barracks and shelter for women and children.

source.title: Alte Feste
source.quote: This fortress served as a barracks and shelter for women and children during the 1904 Herero war.

timeline.claim: Faster growth as settlers arrive from Germany and South Africa.

source.title: History and Heritage
source.quote: After 1907, the town developed more rapidly, with more settlers arriving from Germany and South Africa.

timeline.claim: South African troops occupy Windhoek on behalf of Britain, ending German colonial rule.

source.title: History and Heritage
source.quote: South African troops occupied Windhoek on 12 May 1915 on behalf of Britain.

timeline.claim: Police shoot into a protest against forced removal from the Old Location to Katutura; 11 people are killed.

source.title: History of Old Location and Katutura | Namibia
source.quote: The police shot and killed 11 people and some 44 required medical attention.

timeline.claim: The Old Location is officially closed after residents are resettled in Katutura.

source.title: History of Old Location and Katutura | Namibia
source.quote: The Old Location was officially closed on 31 August 1968.

timeline.claim: Independence brings considerable investment to the city centre.

source.title: History and Heritage
source.quote: Namibia's Independence in 1990 brought considerable investment to the city centre.

places.name: Independence Memorial Museum
places.what: A national museum on the anti-colonial and independence struggle. It opened in 2014 and shows this history across three galleries.

source.title: Independence Museum
source.quote: inaugurated on 20 March 2014

facts.label: Purpose
facts.value: Dedicated to the anti-colonial and independence struggle

source.title: Independence Memorial Museum
source.quote: The museum was opened on 20 March 2014 and it is dedicated to the country’s anti colonial and independence struggle.

facts.label: Galleries
facts.value: Three galleries on resistance and armed liberation struggle

source.title: Independence Museum
source.quote: showcases these aspects throughout three galleries

facts.label: View
facts.value: Glass elevator on the outside of the building with views over the city

source.title: Independence Memorial Museum
source.quote: taking the glass elevator up the outside of the building for great views out over Windhoek

places.name: Heroes' Acre
places.what: The national memorial to the liberation struggle, on the south side of Windhoek. It was inaugurated in 2002.

source.title: Heroes' Acre
source.quote: inaugurated by His Excellency, Dr. Sam Nujoma, Founding President of the Republic of Namibia, on 26 August 2002

facts.label: Design
facts.value: Designed by North Korean experts with the City of Windhoek

source.title: Heroes' Acre
source.quote: designed by a team of North Korean experts, in collaboration with the City of Windhoek

source.title: Heroes' Acre
source.quote: situated between two hills, creating an impressive ambience for the visitor

places.name: Namibia Craft Centre (Old Breweries building)
places.what: A craft shop in the former brewery building on Tal Street. It sells work from artists and crafters.

source.title: Namibia Craft Centre Where Creativity Comes To Life
source.author: Netumbo Nekomba
source.quote: Officially opened in 1990 under Newveld Ventures

facts.label: Building
facts.value: Old Breweries building on Tal Street

source.title: Namibia Craft Centre Where Creativity Comes To Life
source.author: Netumbo Nekomba
source.quote: nestled in the Old Breweries building along Tal Street in Windhoek

source.title: Old Brewery on the corner of Sam Nujoma and Tal Streets
source.quote: it was dedicated on May 12, 1902

facts.label: Later planned role
facts.value: Alte Feste to host a new Craft Centre location and the National Genocide Museum

source.title: Germany Supports Renovation of the Alte Feste Building
source.quote: a new location for the Namibia Craft Centre and the National Genocide Museum

places.name: National Art Gallery of Namibia
places.what: The national art gallery, with a permanent collection and changing exhibitions. It aims to preserve and encourage art in Namibia.

facts.label: Goal
facts.value: Preserve and encourage art in Namibia

source.title: National Art Gallery
source.quote: the goal of this institution is to preserve and encourage art in Namibia.

source.title: National Art Gallery
source.quote: hosts contemporary exhibitions of Regional, National and International Art.

source.title: Vision, Mission and Values
source.quote: It was founded in 1990.

source.title: Vision, Mission and Values
source.quote: It displays in a permanent exhibition of Namibian, African and European Art.

places.name: Daan Viljoen Game Park
places.what: A small game park in the Khomas Hochland west of the city. It is home to springbok, kudu and mountain zebra.

source.title: Daan Viljoen Game Park
source.quote: Just 24 km west of Windhoek lies a sanctuary.

source.title: Daan Viljoen Game Park
source.quote: 40 km²

source.title: Daan Viljoen Game Park
source.quote: Proclamation: Daan Viljoen Game Park 1968

facts.label: Mammals
facts.value: Springbok, kudu, eland, gemsbok, wildebeest, Hartmann's mountain zebra, leopard, klipspringer

source.title: Daan Viljoen Game Park
source.quote: Mammals are springbok, kudu, eland, gemsbok, blue wildebeest, Hartmann's mountain zebra, leopard and klipspringer.

myth.claim: Windhoek simply means 'windy corner' in Afrikaans.
myth.truth: The origin is disputed. The City of Windhoek says some believe Jonker Afrikaner named it after the Winterhoek Mountains in South Africa. Older Nama and Herero names referred to the hot springs.

source.title: History and Heritage
source.quote: Some believe that Afrikaner named Windhoek after the Winterhoek Mountains near Tulbagh in South Africa
